verses.verse:
अन्तः परिधिमानेन मुखरात् षड्गुणाधिकम्।
नवतो न्यूनमित्येव मायतिः सुपरीक्षिता।।१४।।
verses.text: By the measure of the inner circumference, a length from the mouth-hole of more than six times and less than nine [times] has been well tested.

commentary.text: First of all I have to fix the parimāṇa (measure) of the length of the bamboo or pipe, which is to be related to its width. So now I am going to do just that, because every person is three and a half hāth (hastas, cubits) tall by his own hand. This is easier with a pipe, because its width is the same throughout; a bamboo is wider at one end. So the width of the bamboo that counts will be the greater one.

So, to measure that width from inside, roll a piece of thick paper like a chhallā (ring) and put it into the pipe, and see that inside it fits the roundness of the pipe exactly and that the two edges of the paper meet; then take it out. As soon as it comes out, the paper will open out into a length, and just this will be taken as the inner width of the pipe (antaḥ paridhimāna, measure of the inner circumference), because I have to find the width of the body of air inside the pipe. Now let the length of the pipe be measured with the length of that paper: if it is from nine times to eight times, [it is] best; from eight to seven times, middling; and from seven to six times, poor. If it is less than even six times, it will not make a bānsurī. Now, what objection can there be if the length is less or more than this regular measure? For that, attend to the following śloka -
